thought: Repro isolate: gradient ring flickers on Android when animating sweep with useValue. Confirm if redraw is driven by useComputedValue or reanimated shared value bridge.
performance_consideration: Avoid recreating Paint/Shader each frame; cache via useMemo and update uniforms only.
visual_effect: Smooth rotating sweep gradient around a circular stroke, no stutter during fast rotation.

thought: Check if flicker correlates with layout passes: are we reading width/height from onLayout and feeding into Skia nodes each tick? If so, stabilize with derived values.
animation_technique: Derived values for dimensions; avoid state churn
performance_consideration: Don’t set React state every frame; keep animated params in Skia values or Reanimated shared values.
code_snippet: const size=useMemo(()=>({w:canvasW,h:canvasH}),[canvasW,canvasH]); // ensure not changing per frame
visual_effect: No intermittent blank frames when orientation changes or parent rerenders.

thought: Try switching to useClockValue + useDerivedValue (reanimated) driving a Skia value via useSharedValueEffect to reduce JS thread involvement on Android.
animation_technique: Reanimated shared value -> Skia via useSharedValueEffect
performance_consideration: Keep animation on UI thread; JS stalls can show as flicker if shader recreated from JS.
visual_effect: Consistent 60fps rotation even during heavy JS work.

thought: If flicker persists, inspect blend mode / clear: Canvas default clears; but using <Group layer> with opacity might trigger offscreen. Test removing layer and using direct Path stroke.
animation_technique: Avoid offscreen layers; direct draw commands
performance_consideration: Offscreen layers allocate textures; can cause GPU hiccups on mid-tier devices.
code_snippet: // remove <Group layer> and draw <Path style="stroke" strokeWidth={w} color="..." />
visual_effect: No sudden dim/flash frames; stroke remains stable during opacity tweaks.

thought: Potential culprit: creating colors/positions arrays inline. Ensure arrays are stable; otherwise shader rebuild each render. Move to useMemo and reuse Float32Array for positions.
animation_technique: Memoize shader inputs; typed arrays for stops
performance_consideration: Avoid GC pressure from new arrays per render; shader rebuilds can stutter.
visual_effect: Rotation remains fluid; no micro-hitches every few seconds.

thought: Validate on Pixel 6 vs Samsung A52: if only Adreno shows issue, try precompiling runtime effects or simplify shader (no alpha ramps). Capture systrace GPU spikes.
performance_consideration: Some GPUs choke on complex gradients + offscreen; reduce overdraw and shader complexity.
code_snippet: // temporarily swap SweepGradient for SolidColor to confirm shader is culprit
visual_effect: Either confirms shader path or rules it out; should show stable solid ring if GPU OK.

thought: Adopt UI-thread driven shared value + memoized shader inputs. Remove offscreen layer. Add perf guard: skip updates when appState background. This should eliminate flicker.
performance_consideration: Throttle updates when not visible; keep allocations near zero during animation.
visual_effect: Clean rotating ring without flashing; stable battery use when backgrounded.

thought: Need a springy card flip with Skia 3D-ish feel. Approach: animate rotationY and fake perspective via scaleX + shadow/gradient; Skia lacks true 3D transform matrix in nodes.
performance_consideration: Keep transforms in Skia values; avoid wrapping with Animated.View plus Canvas to prevent double compositing.
visual_effect: Card appears to flip with slight squash and lighting shift at mid-rotation.

thought: Use two drawings (front/back). Crossfade around 90° to avoid mirrored text. Drive opacity with cos rotation; clamp near edges to prevent flicker on exact 0/1.
performance_consideration: Render both faces but keep text cached (Picture) to avoid rerasterization each frame.
visual_effect: Front fades out as it turns; back fades in smoothly after passing edge-on.

thought: Try using a RuntimeEffect for perspective warp (barrel-ish) based on x coord and rotation. Might be overkill but could sell depth.
performance_consideration: RuntimeEffect can be expensive on low-end GPUs; watch fragment complexity and avoid branching.
visual_effect: Subtle perspective bend as card rotates, like a real physical card.

thought: Revision: skip RuntimeEffect. Better: fake lighting with a moving linear gradient overlay tied to rotation. Much cheaper and close enough visually.
animation_technique: Gradient lighting overlay tied to rotation
performance_consideration: Gradients are cheaper than custom fragment shader; keep overlay in same draw pass to reduce overdraw.
code_snippet: const gx=useComputedValue(()=>cx+Math.sin(r.current)*w*0.3,[r]); // use LinearGradient start/end around gx
visual_effect: Specular highlight sweeps across card during flip; maintains crisp text.

thought: Branch: add tap-to-flip with spring. Use Reanimated with withSpring and pipe to Skia via useSharedValueEffect. Ensure hitSlop stays in React layer; Canvas just renders.
performance_consideration: Avoid bridging per-frame from JS; only set target values on tap, let UI thread animate.
visual_effect: Snappy spring flip on tap, no dropped frames when tapping repeatedly.

thought: Finalize: main branch uses dual-face + gradient lighting; interaction branch adds spring trigger. Add clamp near 90° to prevent both faces visible. Ship with feature flag.
performance_consideration: Clamp opacity around edge-on to avoid alpha blending cost spikes; pre-record text as Picture.
visual_effect: Convincing flip with highlight, readable faces, and responsive tap interaction.

thought: Investigate janky Lottie-to-Skia port: path morph animation spikes CPU. Suspect rebuilding Path each frame. Consider recording to Picture or using Path.interpolate if available.
performance_consideration: Path ops on JS thread are expensive; precompute points and update only transforms.
code_snippet: // avoid: const p=Skia.Path.MakeFromSVGString(d)! inside computed value; cache base paths and lerp points
visual_effect: Morph stays smooth at 30–60fps without periodic freezes.

thought: Add profiling: wrap Canvas in <FPSGraph/> and log frame durations. If spikes align with GC, reduce allocations in computed values and prefer typed arrays for point lists.
performance_consideration: Computed values that allocate arrays each tick will trigger GC and hitching.
code_snippet: const pts=useMemo(()=>new Float32Array(N*2),[]); // update in-place; avoid map()/spread
visual_effect: Frame time graph flattens; fewer long frames above 24ms.

thought: Branch experiment: move morph math to a worklet; send only t plus two point buffers to Skia. If bridge costs, keep everything in Skia and animate with clock value.
performance_consideration: Keep heavy math off JS; avoid copying large arrays over the bridge each frame.
code_snippet: // in worklet: for(i=0;i<n;i++) out[i]=a[i]+(b[i]-a[i])*t; then write into shared array
visual_effect: Morph remains smooth even when JS thread is busy (navigation, logs).

thought: Tried Path.op union each frame to fill overlaps; it looked cool but totally tanks performance. Not worth keeping in the plan.
performance_consideration: Path.op is heavy and forces complex tessellation; will drop frames on most devices.
visual_effect: Would have produced a gooey merge effect, but causes visible stutter and heat.

thought: Conclusion: cache base geometry, interpolate points in-place (worklet optional), avoid Path ops. Validate on low-end Moto G Power. Add fallback to 30fps if CPU > 70%.
animation_technique: In-place point lerp + cached draw commands
performance_consideration: Graceful degradation: cap FPS under sustained load; prevents thermal throttling.
code_snippet: // simple cap: if(avgFrameMs>28) setTargetFps(30); else setTargetFps(60);
visual_effect: Morph animation stays stable; slightly less smooth under load but no long freezes.
